editorial.headline: Cross-Border Routes, Open to Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: This route-based, city-to-city cross-border transport activity is open nationally to full foreign ownership and is not caught by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Angkutan Lintas Batas Negara is a route-bound form of transport: movement from one city to another that crosses a national border as part of an established route. The classification turns on that concrete pattern of movement. A city-to-city journey, the crossing of a frontier, and a route to which the service is tied are all present in its stated scope. Read together, those elements give the activity its operating identity: cross-border transport conducted along a route, rather than a loose reference to travel that happens to reach another country.

Its registration window is not confined to one end of the business-size range. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises. That is a deliberately practical point: the classification is not reserved for a single scale of operator. The activity must still match its stated route-based, cross-border scope, but the record places it across all four listed business categories. For a founder, scale is therefore an eligibility statement in the classification, not a reason to dilute the definition of the activity itself.

Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The implication is plain: full foreign ownership is permitted at the national level. A 100% ceiling is not a partial cap; the national entry allows foreign capital up to complete ownership. The record cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the source for that position. This is the national baseline from which the Bali question has to be assessed—without adding conditions that the record does not supply.

Bali deserves an equally direct reading. The province’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`, and the record states that at the Besar scale its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, meaning it is not blocked by that moratorium. The central fact is simple: full national foreign ownership is permitted, and Bali does not block PMA registration under its moratorium. For this activity, Bali is an available place to register rather than an exception to national PMA openness.
